Description - RemoveFolder

Deletes a folder.

Force semantics (live): force=false refuses only folders that contain files (NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder); a folder that contains only subfolders is deleted together with them and status is Ok. force=true deletes files and subfolders. Unknown or already removed ids give NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder with force=false. Caveat (exploration, not captured): an already removed id with force=true returned Ok, so Ok does not prove that something was deleted.

Client behaviour: on NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder the client asks the user and may resend with force=true.

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/RemoveFolder. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/RemoveFolder) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/RemoveFolder (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation RemoveFolder. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/RemoveFolder query.

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check RemoveFolderResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema RemoveFolderResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required RemoveFolderResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for RemoveFolder: <s:Envelope><s:Body><RemoveFolderResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><RemoveFolderResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <RemoveFolderResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <RemoveFolderResult> object required StatusResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <a:status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. The client accepts only Ok; BadToken triggers a re-login, anything else is an error.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <a:errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise.

500 SoapFault

WCF SOAP fault (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, not compressed). Possible for every SOAP operation: an empty or malformed body gives a:InternalServiceFault, an undeserialisable value a:DeserializationFailed, an unknown or missing SOAPAction a:ActionNotSupported. Operations with an operation-specific captured fault document it inline instead.

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • Result has only status/errorMessage (no prevModifyTime/modifyTime).
  • force=false still deletes folders whose content is only subfolders.

Security notes - findings that concern RemoveFolder

  • S-04 Medium (data loss) RemoveFolder force=false only protects folders that contain files; a folder holding only subfolders is deleted with all of them, status Ok.

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
